items.text: NPR confirmed the three core unresolved issues ahead of the second Islamabad round: (1) Nuclear enrichment — the US demands Iran commit to never seeking a nuclear weapon or the tools for one; Iran says it will "never accept" being an "exception from international law" on enrichment. military.t: VANCE DEPARTED for Islamabad — Axios: 3 US Sources Confirmed. Talks Tonight.
military.d: Axios (three US sources, Tuesday): VP Vance departed for Islamabad by Tuesday morning for a second round of talks to end the West Asia War. CNN live confirmed US officials expected to depart today. Pakistan in full lockdown — 10,000 security forces, Serena Hotel prepared, all protocol in place. Ceasefire expires tonight at 1:30 AM IST Wednesday. Trump could allow informal extension if talks show progress — he already extended from Tuesday to Wednesday evening ET. Vance leading with Witkoff and Kushner as in round one. Critical question: will the Iranian delegation arrive before or after the ceasefire technically expires? If Iran arrives and begins indirect talks: Trump will almost certainly hold fire even if the clock runs out.

military.t: Iran: No Delegation Yet (State TV) — But AP + MS NOW: They WILL Come If Vance Is There.
military.d: Iran state TV Tuesday: "So far, no delegation from Iran has departed for Islamabad, whether main or subsidiary, primary or secondary." BUT — AP (two regional officials): Iranian negotiators will attend. MS NOW (foreign diplomat in Tehran with close contact to Ghalibaf): Ghalibaf and FM Araghchi will travel to Islamabad, but ONLY IF Vance is personally present. Vance has confirmed going. Axios: the White House spent all of Monday waiting for Tehran signal — delayed by IRGC pressure on negotiators to hold firm on blockade. This internal power struggle between Iran's diplomatic corps and IRGC is the real story. If IRGC pressure yields to diplomatic pragmatism: Iran shows up. If IRGC wins the internal argument: Iran doesn't come and war resumes.

military.t: IRGC Blocking Iran Diplomats — Pressuring "No Talks Without Lifting Blockade" (Axios).
military.d: Axios (person with knowledge of White House deliberations): "The Iranians were stalling amid apparent pressure from the Revolutionary Guards on the negotiators to hold a firmer line: no talks without lifting the blockade." This is the most significant piece of intelligence on the talks. Iran's IRGC — which has its own navy, confirmed it rearmed during the ceasefire, and called Touska seizure "piracy" — is not aligned with the Foreign Ministry position on talks. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf serves as a bridge figure: he is both a political figure with IRGC roots AND the designated negotiator. His statement about "new battlefield cards" reflected IRGC pressure. Whether he ultimately travels to Islamabad reflects the outcome of this internal struggle.

military.t: WH Leavitt: "Never Been So Close." Trump CNBC: "Going to End Up With a Great Deal."

Trump told CNBC's Squawk Box Tuesday morning: "What I think is that we're going to end up with a great deal." Brent crude fell slightly on the CNBC comment. These are the most optimistic public signals from the US side since the West Asia War began February 28. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi told Pakistan's Dar that Iran is "taking all aspects into consideration and will decide on how to proceed" — careful language that neither fully confirms nor denies. The two sides' diplomatic signals are more aligned than their military postures suggest. A deal framework — not a final agreement, but an extension + framework — is within reach if talks begin.

military.t: Three Unresolved Sticking Points — Nuclear, Blockade, Lebanon. NPR Analysis.
military.d: NPR confirmed the three core gaps heading into Islamabad round two: (1) Nuclear enrichment: US demands Iran commit to never pursuing nuclear weapons or the tools for them; Iran refuses to accept being an "exception from international law." US proposed 20-year pause at round one; Iran countered with 5 years; Trump said even 20 years was "unacceptable." (2) US naval blockade: Iran says blockade must end before productive talks can happen; US says blockade stays until a deal is done. This is a classic chicken-and-egg deadlock. (3) Lebanon: Iran insists any deal must include ceasefire in Lebanon; US and Israel have consistently refused. Additionally, Iran demands $20B+ in frozen assets and war reparations; US position is much lower. A senior Iranian source told Reuters Iran is also not open to discussing its missile programme. Round two aims for a framework and extension — not resolution of all four issues.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 7:15 PM IST. Vance is in the air. The ceasefire expires in 6 hours.

THE STATE OF PLAY
• Vance departed for Islamabad — Axios, 3 US sources confirmed
• Iran state TV: "no delegation departed yet as of Tuesday"
• AP (2 regional officials): Iranian negotiators WILL attend
• MS NOW (diplomat in Tehran with Ghalibaf contact): Ghalibaf + Araghchi go IF Vance present
• Vance IS present — so the condition is technically met
• The question is timing: will they arrive before the ceasefire expires at 1:30 AM IST?

THE OPTIMISM SIGNALS
• WH Leavitt (Mon Fox News): "Never been so close to a truly good deal"
• Trump (Tue CNBC Squawk Box): "Going to end up with a great deal"
• Brent fell slightly on Trump CNBC comment — markets believe it
• Sensex +753 today, third consecutive session of gains
• India markets pricing in 55-60% probability of ceasefire extension

THE BLOCKING FORCE — IRGC
• Axios (White House source): IRGC pressuring Iranian negotiators to hold firm: no talks without lifting blockade
• This explains the gap between Iran's private signals (coming) and public face (refusing)
• Ghalibaf is both the lead negotiator AND has IRGC roots — his decision reflects this internal struggle
• If IRGC yields to diplomatic pragmatism: Iran delegation boards the flight
• If IRGC wins: Iran doesn't come, ceasefire lapses, military response within hours

THE MILITARY DIMENSION
• Iran Gen. Abdollahi (top joint military command): "prepared to respond decisively"
• IRGC confirmed rearmed faster than pre-war pace
• Three US carrier battle groups in theatre: Lincoln (Gulf of Oman), Ford (Red Sea), Bush (converging)
• Both sides are more militarily ready for escalation today than on February 28

THE THREE GAPS
• Nuclear enrichment: US wants no enrichment ever; Iran says unacceptable
• Blockade: Iran wants it lifted first; US says only after deal
• Lebanon: Iran insists it's included; US/Israel refuse

INDIA'S POSITION TONIGHT
• Sensex 79,273 — up 753, third consecutive gain
• Rupee ~94.00 — stable on deal optimism
• Brent $95.38 — moderated from Monday spike
• India VIX still elevated at ~19 — markets not fully at ease
• Tonight 1:30 AM IST: the moment of truth
• If extension: Wednesday Sensex 80,000-82,000+, India VIX 15-17
• If lapses: Wednesday Sensex 73,000-75,000, Brent $108-120, rupee 97+
• Infosys results also Wednesday — dual event, dual risk

VERDICT: Vance is in the air. Iran's diplomatic corps wants to come. The IRGC wants to hold firm. Pakistan, Egypt, China, Turkey are all pushing Iran to the table. The 753-point Sensex rally says the market thinks the IRGC loses this argument. The 6 hours between now and the ceasefire expiry will answer the question that has defined the West Asia War for 53 days: can diplomacy beat military logic at the last hour?
